traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 93 Capparidaceae: trees, shrubs or more rarely herbs, sometimes climbing; leaves alternate, rarely opposite, simple or palmately of 3 to 7 leaflets; stipules minute or spiny where present; flowers mostly bisexual, regular or rarely irregular; sepals usually 4, petals 4 to many or none; stamens few to many; ovary superior, usually on a stalk (gynophore); fruit a capsule or a berry. Hutchinson's family also holds the herbaceous Cleome and kin that APG sets apart as Cleomaceae; Capparaceae itself is mostly woody (Library 1.0: 85% shrubs and trees).

traits.stamens.note: Wikipedia, Caper (read 2026-10-16): stamens many, long. The order's typical 6 would draw caper flowers wrongly.

traits.leaf_habit.note: Wikipedia, Caper (read 2026-10-16): thick shiny leaves on a perennial shrub; evergreen inferred.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Wikipedia Capparis (read 2026-10-17) (largest genus, ~140 species): leaves simple and entire.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Wikipedia Capparis (read 2026-10-17): leaves simple, entire. Weighted by Capparis and allies (Morisonia, Maerua, Boscia).

traits.fruit_type.note: Wikipedia Capparis (read 2026-10-17): 146 spp (POWO 2026), the largest genus, fruit a globose or ellipsoid berry. Morisonia (86 spp) and Maerua (70) pages give counts only, no fruit; the family total (~430, first pass's Wikipedia reading) means Capparis alone is about a third. Berry leads on the one genus counted; capsules kept as sometimes for the dry-fruited minority.

traits.leaf_division.note: Wikipedia Capparis (read 2026-10-17): 146 spp, leaves simple and entire. Morisonia (86) and Maerua (70) pages give counts but no leaf form. Simple leads on the largest genus, about a third of ~430 spp; compound kept as sometimes for the foliolate genera such as Crateva (not read).
